label: Claude Haiku 5.5
output:
Our Winter School on Elliptic Curves and Modular Forms wrapped up on Saturday. I'm writing this on behalf of the three of us who organised it: Ketaki Joglekar, Faizan Mirza and me.

The school ran from 5 to 7 November 2026 in Seminar Hall 2, Department of Mathematics, Sahyadri Institute of Science, Pune. We received 112 applications and selected 41 participants, MSc and early PhD students from 9 states. Selection was based on a statement and one reference, so it was competitive, and we were glad to see how much talent applied.

We are grateful to Prof. Anuradha Venkatesan, our faculty mentor, who guided us throughout. Thank you, ma'am.

Our speakers were Dr. Nilesh Dharmadhikari from Hyderabad, who spoke on Mordell-Weil; Dr. Sunanda Iyer from Chennai, who covered modular forms; and Dr. Tomasz Wierzbicki, who joined online from Kraków to teach computations in Sage. Thank you all for giving your time so generously.

The school was funded by a Rs 2.4 lakh grant from the institute's student initiative fund. That covered hostel stay and travel for 18 outstation students, so distance and cost did not decide who could attend. Thank you to the institute for backing the idea.

Mr. Prakash Salunke from the office staff sorted out the hostel rooms at 11 pm when a booking got messed up. We are very grateful. Thanks also to the six PhD students who worked as teaching assistants and ran the problem sessions. That format worked so well that we want to keep it.

Day 2 had a real test. The power went out for nearly two hours in the afternoon, the laptops ran out of battery, and we moved the problem session to the canteen with two rolling whiteboards. Honestly, it turned out to be the best session of the three days. Thanks to everyone who stayed and kept going.

One moment stood out. A student from Silchar found an error in a worked example in Dr. Iyer's notes. The error was corrected live, and the student was thanked for spotting it. That is exactly what a school like this should do. Small schools matter a lot for MSc students because they get room to ask questions, which bigger conferences rarely offer.

To all the participants: thank you for bringing your questions, your curiosity, and your patience with the hiccups.

Slides and problem sheets will be uploaded to the department website within two weeks. We hope to run a second edition in late 2027, subject to funding. If you would like to be kept in the loop, feel free to message me.
